#73Linux (Pi 5 / Trixie fork)
## I want to stress, I am in no way, shape, or form, a programmer. This was generated by grok-ai by pulling KM4ACK's 73Linux Git and updating the script to be used on CM5/Debian Trixie. KM4ACK dropped support for Raspberry Pi's, with more desire to work on x86_64 systems. 73Linux is great for the ClockworkPi uConsole for a portable Station, using a Xeigu X6200 or a QRP-Labs QMX. It also makes quick deployment on a portable ARM device amazing. I will update this when I fully test the script and test each install. Scrutinize this as much as possible. Please fork, optimize, and take it further for yourself and/or those with Raspberry Pi based Radio Go-Bags.



**This copy restores Raspberry Pi support for Raspberry Pi 5 running Debian 13 / Raspberry Pi OS Trixie.** Official 73Linux dropped Pi support in 4.1.9. Read PI5_TRIXIE.md first.

## Description

73 Linux supports Raspberry Pi (aarch64 / armv7l) and x86_64 Debian based systems. You choose which ham radio applications to install.

This is an **unofficial fork**. Original project: [km4ack/73Linux](https://github.com/km4ack/73Linux) by Jason Oleham, KM4ACK.

# Install on a Pi 5 (Trixie)

```bash
sudo apt update && sudo apt full-upgrade -y
sudo apt install -y git yad jq bc curl wget
sudo raspi-config   # Advanced Options -> Wayland -> X11, then reboot
sudo usermod -aG dialout,tty,plugdev,gpio "$USER"
# log out / reboot

git clone https://github.com/CzarD0mn/73Linux-pi5-trixie.git $HOME/73Linux-pi5-trixie
bash $HOME/73Linux-pi5-trixie/bootstrap.sh
# 73Linux is installed to your user home, e.g. /home/pi/73Linux
bash $HOME/73Linux/73.sh
```

Keep `.pi5-trixie-fork` in the tree so 73.sh does not replace itself with upstream.
